title: Scraper: Extend Gigabyte to Threadripper / Threadripper Pro
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Extend the existing GigabyteScraper to cover sTRX4 (TRX40), sTR5 (TRX50), sWRX8 (WRX80), and sWRX9 (WRX90 forthcoming) board lines.

board_class: Threadripper, ThreadripperPro.

Gigabyte boards in scope:
- sTRX4: TRX40 AORUS XTREME, TRX40 AORUS PRO WIFI, TRX40 DESIGNARE
- sTR5: TRX50 AERO D, TRX50 AORUS XTREME
- sWRX8: WRX80-SU8-IPMI (workstation/server hybrid)
- sWRX9: forthcoming WRX90 SKUs

Implementation:
- src/psp_etl/scrape/gigabyte.py has _SOCKET_URLS = {'AM4': '...All-Series/AM4', 'AM5': '...All-Series/AM5'}. Confirm the URL pattern for TR/TR-Pro: Gigabyte typically uses 'TR4'/'sTRX4'/'TRX40' as path segments — try https://www.gigabyte.com/Motherboard/All-Series/TRX40 first, then TRX50/WRX80/WRX90.
- The Akamai bot-detection considerations from the existing scraper apply unchanged.
- Per-board page parsing (BeautifulSoup) likely works without changes — same support tab structure.

Note on overlap with Gigabyte server (#83):
- WRX80-SU8-IPMI lives on www.gigabyte.com (consumer) but is workstation. MZ-prefixed boards on Enterprise/Server-Motherboard are EPYC. Keep these separate: this issue covers the consumer-tree workstation; #83 covers the enterprise-tree server.

Acceptance criteria:
- Existing AM4/AM5 tests pass
- New tests for at least one TRX40 and one WRX80 board parse
- Updated _SOCKET_URLS plus socket-detection update

Related: #79, #81.
